parsed.main_gap: Lemma 1 and the 'infinite sunflower fact' are stated for unbounded finite sets, where both are false; only the bounded-size (|C| ≤ K) case is needed and is correct.

errors.description: The 'elementary infinite sunflower fact' is false for families of finite sets of unbounded size (e.g. the chain {1},{1,2},{1,2,3},... has no infinite Δ-subsystem), and the sketched induction ('delete that element, and continue') need not terminate. Consequently Lemma 1 as stated (no size bound) is false. The argument is valid only under a uniform size bound, which is all that is actually used ('|C| ≤ K', terminal members have |D| ≤ a_1); the repair is to add that hypothesis and note termination after ≤ K deletions.

parsed.notes: Structure is sound: acceptance depends only on prime support; F is self-dual; minimal supports C form an intersecting antichain; Lemma 2's weight descent (via the coprime witness of the rejected squarefree w(E\{p})) bounds every prime to a terminal member of size ≤ a_1; finiteness of C gives periodicity mod L and the count T. Only flaw is the over-general false Lemma 1/sunflower statement.
